claim: The 2La inversion is a widespread polymorphism in the Anopheles gambiae species complex.
source: The 2La inversion is a widespread polymorphism in the Anopheles gambiae species complex, the major African mosquito vectors of human malaria.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by the geographic distribution data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mosquitoes carrying the 2L+a allele are more susceptible to malaria infection than those carrying the 2La allele.
source: Here we show that alleles of the 2La inversion are associated with natural malaria infection levels in wild-captured vectors from West and East Africa.
evidence: This claim is supported by infection prevalence data from Kenya, Guinea-Conakry, and Burkina Faso shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Mosquitoes carrying the 2L+a allele are behaviorally less likely to be found inside houses.
source: Mosquitoes carrying the more-susceptible allele (2L+a) are also behaviorally less likely to be found inside houses.
evidence: This is supported by human landing capture data from Guinea-Conakry presented in Figure 5.

claim: The 2La inversion comprises approximately 10% of the genome size.
source: The 2La inversion comprises ~10% of the genome size and segregates in A. gambiae and A. coluzzii, the only species of the complex in which it is polymorphic.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of the 2La inversion.

claim: The 2La inversion segregates only in A. gambiae and A. coluzzii within the A. gambiae species complex.
source: The 2La inversion comprises ~10% of the genome size and segregates in A. gambiae and A. coluzzii, the only species of the complex in which it is polymorphic.
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of the 2La inversion polymorphism.

claim: There is no inherent difference in P. falciparum susceptibility between A. gambiae and A. coluzzii species.
source: Field-based studies have found no inherent difference in P. falciparum susceptibility between these main vector species of the A. gambiae complex, A. gambiae and A. coluzzii (Fryxell et al., 2012; Gnémé et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous field studies.

claim: The 2La inversion polymorphism has been correlated with adaptation to aridity or humidity.
source: Polymorphism of the 2La inversion has been correlated with aspects of vector bionomics, particularly adaptation to aridity or humidity (Coluzzi et al., 1979; Fouet et al., 2012), and biting and resting behavior (Coluzzi et al., 1977).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: High frequencies of 2L+a are present in humid southern forest and coastal regions of West Africa.
source: An allelic frequency cline was described in West Africa, where high frequencies of 2L+a are present in humid southern forest and coastal regions, with the 2La allele gradually becoming predominant northward, until becoming essentially fixed in the arid sub-Saharan savanna (Coluzzi et al., 1979; Touré et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies describing geographic distribution patterns.

claim: A prior cytogenetic study in Kenya detected that mosquitoes homozygous for 2L+a/2L+a displayed a two-fold higher prevalence of P. falciparum infection than 2La/2La homokaryotypes.
source: In that report, mosquitoes homozygous for the 2L+a/2L+a karyotype displayed a two-fold higher prevalence of P. falciparum infection than sympatric inverted 2La/2La homokaryotypes.
evidence: This refers to findings from a previous study by Petrarca and Beier, 1992.

claim: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the 2L+a/2L+a genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than 2La/2La homozygotes in Kenya.
source: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the homozygous 2L+a/2L+a inversion genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than the 2La/2La homozygotes at all three study sites (Figure 2A, Chi-squared = 11.25, df = 2, p=0.004 for Kenya, Chi-squared = 7.96, df = 2, p=0.02 for Guinea-Conakry and Chi-squared = 33.52, df = 2, p=5*10−8 for Burkina Faso).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of oocyst infection prevalence data from Kenya.

claim: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the 2L+a/2L+a genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than 2La/2La homozygotes in Guinea-Conakry.
source: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the homozygous 2L+a/2L+a inversion genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than the 2La/2La homozygotes at all three study sites (Figure 2A, Chi-squared = 11.25, df = 2, p=0.004 for Kenya, Chi-squared = 7.96, df = 2, p=0.02 for Guinea-Conakry and Chi-squared = 33.52, df = 2, p=5*10−8 for Burkina Faso).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of oocyst infection prevalence data from Guinea-Conakry.

claim: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the 2L+a/2L+a genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than 2La/2La homozygotes in Burkina Faso.
source: A. gambiae complex mosquitoes with the homozygous 2L+a/2L+a inversion genotype were significantly more likely to carry midgut oocysts than the 2La/2La homozygotes at all three study sites (Figure 2A, Chi-squared = 11.25, df = 2, p=0.004 for Kenya, Chi-squared = 7.96, df = 2, p=0.02 for Guinea-Conakry and Chi-squared = 33.52, df = 2, p=5*10−8 for Burkina Faso).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of oocyst infection prevalence data from Burkina Faso.

claim: In Burkina Faso samples, infection intensity was significantly higher in 2L+a/2L+a homozygotes compared to 2La/2La homozygotes.
source: In the Burkina Faso samples, infection intensity was significantly higher in the 2L+a/2L+a homozygotes as compared to 2La/2La homozygotes (p=0.01).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of oocyst intensity data from Burkina Faso.

claim: 2La/2La homozygotes were present at higher frequency in uninfected mosquitoes while 2L+a/2L+a homozygotes were at higher frequency in infected mosquitoes.
source: However, 2La/2La homozygotes were present at higher frequency in uninfected mosquitoes, while 2L+a/2L+a homozygotes were at higher frequency in infected mosquitoes.
evidence: This claim is supported by the analysis of inversion genotype frequencies in infected vs uninfected groups shown in Figure 2C.

claim: There was no significant difference in mosquito life span between 2La/2La and 2L+a/2L+a genotypes in semi-field conditions in Kenya.
source: There was no significant difference in mosquito life span between 2La/2La and 2L+a/2L+a mosquito genotypes in the sympatric population across three replicate experiments (Figure 3, p = 0.478, average median survival across replicates 19.3 days).
evidence: This claim is supported by longevity data from semi-field experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: There was no difference in survival between 2La genotypes following infection with entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium.
source: The virulence of Metarhizium as a pathogen was confirmed by the shortened mosquito lifespan observed across all 2La inversion genotypes (Figure 4, average median survival across replicates 6 days as compared to 19.3 days without fungus exposure in Figure 3), but there was no difference in survival between 2La genotypes following infection with entomopathogenic fungus (Figure 4, p=0.877).
evidence: This claim is supported by fungal infection survival data shown in Figure 4.

claim: 100% of bloodmeals from blood-containing female mosquitoes across all 2La inversion genotypes were human-derived in Guinea-Conakry.
source: Across all 2La inversion genotypes, 100% of bloodmeals from the blood-containing females were human-derived (total n = 210, 2L+a/2L+a n = 69, 2L+a/2La n = 72, 2La/2La n = 69).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular bloodmeal analysis data from Guinea-Conakry.

claim: 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes are less likely than 2La/2La genotypes to be captured indoors attracted to human bait in Guinea-Conakry.
source: First, 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes are less likely than 2La/2La genotypes to be captured indoors attracted to human bait, suggesting that 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes are less likely than 2La/2La to feed inside habitations. The deficit of 2L+a/2L+a homozygotes among indoor captured mosquitoes was significant (double asterisks in Figure 5, Chi-squared = 6.99, df = 1, p=0.008, for the fraction of 2L+a/2L+a caught on HLC indoor versus caught on all other methods, as compared to the same fraction for 2La/2La).
evidence: This claim is supported by human landing capture data from Guinea-Conakry shown in Figure 5.

claim: Proportionally fewer 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes were captured by human landing capture overall relative to their representation in larval site frequencies in Guinea-Conakry.
source: Thus, proportionally fewer 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes were captured by HLC overall (HLC outdoor and indoor combined), relative to their total representation in the population based on larval site frequencies (2L+a/2L+a were 27% of total HLC versus 42% of total larvae). This under-representation in adult population sampling of 2L+a/2L+a genotypes as compared to 2La/2La was also significant (Chi-squared = 5.92, df = 1, p=0.02).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of adult capture data with larval sampling data from Guinea-Conakry shown in Figure 5.

claim: The 2La inversion has a monophyletic origin.
source: All windows displayed phylogenetic patterns consistent with monophyly (Figure 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic analysis of genome sequences shown in Figure 6.

claim: For genomic windows spanning the inversion breakpoints and central to the inversion, individuals cluster predominantly by 2La genotype regardless of geographic origin.
source: For the two windows spanning the inversion breakpoints and the one window central to the inversion, all individuals cluster predominantly by 2La genotype regardless of their geographic origin, despite apparent geographic substructure visible in some samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic tree analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: For genomic windows outside the 2La inversion, samples cluster by geographic origin rather than by 2La genotype.
source: In contrast, the control windows (one outside the inversion on the left arm of chromosome 2L, and one on each of the arms of chromosome 3) displayed a pattern of clustering based mostly on geographic origin of the samples.
evidence: This claim is supported by phylogenetic tree analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: There is a strong positive correlation between the frequency of the 2L+a allele and annual precipitation.
source: There is a strong positive correlation between the frequency of the 2L+a allele and annual precipitation (Figure 7, r2 = 0.86).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis of 2L+a frequency and precipitation data shown in Figure 7.

claim: When A. gambiae and A. coluzzii taxa were analyzed individually, each still displayed high positive correlation of 2L+a frequency with annual rainfall.
source: The genotype data included two taxa, A. gambiae and A. coluzzii, and examination of the taxa individually, although generating smaller sample sizes, nevertheless still demonstrated a strong positive correlation between 2L+a allele and annual precipitation (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 A. gambiae r2 = 0.857, A. coluzzii r2 = 0.999).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The 2La inversion is the only frequent and widespread natural genetic polymorphism with significant influence on P. falciparum infection rates in the vector population.
source: Thus, based on results of the current study, the 2La inversion is, to our knowledge, the only frequent and widespread natural genetic polymorphism with significant influence on P. falciparum infection rates in the vector population.
evidence: This claim is based on comparison with previous genetic association studies and the current findings.

claim: The association of malaria infection and 2La inversion genotype is probably due to a common underlying genetic mechanism throughout Africa.
source: The association of malaria infection and 2La inversion genotype is probably due to a common underlying genetic mechanism throughout Africa rather than a series of local adaptations, because of the monophyletic origin of the 2La inversion within the A. gambiae species complex, and the Africa-wide distribution of the allele-phenotype association.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the monophyletic origin data and the consistent association across geographic sites.

claim: The mechanism of differential infection of 2La inversion genotypes is at least partly based on genetically controlled physiological differences for parasite development efficiency.
source: The mechanism of differential infection of 2La inversion genotypes is at least partly based on genetically controlled physiological differences for parasite development efficiency in 2L+a/2L+a as compared to 2La/2La mosquitoes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the membrane feeding experiment results in Burkina Faso which controlled for behavioral factors.

claim: The molecular mechanism of differential susceptibility must be relatively specifically addressed to P. falciparum because 2La genotypes do not display detectable differences in general immune competence.
source: The molecular mechanism of differential susceptibility must be relatively specifically addressed to P. falciparum, because the 2La genotypes do not display detectable differences in general immune competence.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the longevity and fungal infection experiments showing no difference in survival or immune response.

claim: The inversion alleles are non-recombining haplotypes carrying approximately 2000 genes.
source: The inversion alleles are non-recombining haplotypes carrying ~2000 genes.
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the 2La inversion structure.

claim: Genetic mapping in wild pedigrees from homozygous 2La/2La crosses in Mali identified a cluster of quantitative trait loci linked to oocyst infection prevalence within the proximal 2La inversion breakpoint.
source: Genetic mapping carried out in wild pedigrees from homozygous 2La/2La crosses in Mali identified a cluster of quantitative trait loci (QTL) linked to oocyst infection prevalence (Niaré et al., 2002; Riehle et al., 2006). The cluster is located within the proximal 2La inversion breakpoint, and the region was termed the Plasmodium Resistance Island.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous genetic mapping studies.

claim: The APL1 gene family of leucine-rich repeat proteins display a protective phenotype for Plasmodium infection prevalence in functional assays.
source: Within the resistance island, the APL1 gene family of leucine-rich repeat (LRR) proteins display a protective phenotype for Plasmodium infection prevalence in functional assays (Mitri et al., 2009; Riehle et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claim: LRIM1 is located within the 2La inversion.
source: Another LRR immune factor, LRIM1, is also located within the 2La inversion, and additional nearby LRR genes with a similar protective phenotype for P. falciparum were recently identified (Mitri et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is stated as a known location of the LRIM1 gene.

claim: The most likely explanation for the observed behavioral results is that 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes are significantly more exophilic and 2La/2La more endophilic.
source: The most likely explanation for the observed behavioral results is that 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes are significantly more exophilic, and 2La/2La more endophilic.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the human landing capture and larval sampling data.

claim: The only previous test of association of the 2La inversion with endophilic or exophilic behavior in northern Nigeria found that 2L+a carriers were less likely than 2La carriers to be captured indoors.
source: Second, the only previous test of association of the 2La inversion with endophilic or exophilic behavior, in northern Nigeria, found that 2L+a carriers were less likely than 2La carriers to be captured indoors (Coluzzi et al., 1979), which is consistent with the current results.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Carriage of the 2L+a/2L+a genotype is a hallmark of the sylvan-adapted Forest chromosomal form.
source: Third, carriage of the 2L+a/2L+a genotype is a hallmark of the sylvan-adapted Forest chromosomal form (Coluzzi et al., 1979), which was observed to be highly exophilic and human-biting (Bockarie et al., 1993, 1994).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: In western Kenya, the 2L+a/2L+a frequency increased from 0% detectable in 1994 before ITN rollout to 66% by 2011 after rollout.
source: In the only examination of 2La genotypes under indoor selection pressure to our knowledge, the 2L+a/2L+a frequency increased from 0% detectable in 1994 before ITN rollout in western Kenya to 66% by 2011 after rollout (Matoke-Muhia et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The 2La inversion is not genetically associated with resistance to pyrethroid insecticides used on ITNs.
source: The 2La inversion is not genetically associated with resistance to the pyrethroid insecticides used on ITNs (Brooke et al., 2002), so the underlying mechanism is more likely to be behavioral avoidance rather than chemical selection.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study and inference about the mechanism.

claim: At the time of the current collections in Guinea-Conakry, the country had the lowest use of ITNs in Africa.
source: At the time of the current collections in Guinea-Conakry, the country had the lowest use of ITNs in Africa (President's Malaria Initiative, 2014), which provides the opportunity to monitor 2L+a allele frequencies there as ITNs are rolled out.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a report.

claim: Proxies for humidity (high annual rainfall and vegetation density) were the covariates most strongly correlated with P. falciparum parasite rate.
source: Examination of ecological correlates found that proxies for humidity (high annual rainfall and vegetation density) were the covariates most strongly correlated with PfPR (Weiss et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The 2L+a allele generally correlates geographically with humidity.
source: The 2L+a allele generally correlates geographically with humidity (Coluzzi et al., 1979; Cheng et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The highest P. falciparum parasite rate in Guinea-Conakry is in the southern forested zone, where about 85-90% of the 5-14 year-old group was P. falciparum-positive during 2011-2013.
source: However, the highest PfPR in Guinea-Conakry is in the southern forested zone, where about 85–90% of the 5–14 year-old group was P. falciparum-positive during the period 2011–2013 (Tiffany et al., 2016), near the current study sites of Koraboh and Koundara where vector populations displayed the highest 2L+a frequencies of up to 57%, while in the northern humid savanna the 2L+a frequency decreased to 27% and in the arid savanna, 4% (Coulibaly et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Chromosome inversions suppress genetic recombination and establish co-adapted gene complexes, or supergenes.
source: Chromosome inversions suppress genetic recombination and establish co-adapted gene complexes, or supergenes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about chromosome inversions.

claim: Inversions are physical rearrangements of a chromosome segment that suppress recombination and limit exchange of variation between two alternate suites of alleles.
source: Inversions are physical rearrangements of a chromosome segment that suppress recombination and limit exchange of variation between two alternate suites of alleles.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about inversions.

claim: Diverged adaptive gene complexes from inversions function as supergenes in many organisms.
source: These diverged adaptive gene complexes function as supergenes in many organisms (Thompson and Jiggins, 2014) and influence diverse phenotypes including butterfly color mimicry (Joron et al., 2011; Nishikawa et al., 2015), ant colonial behavior (Wang et al., 2013), avian reproductive morphs (Lamichhaney et al., 2016; Huynh et al., 2011), human fertility (Stefansson et al., 2005), and Drosophila ecological adaptation (Corbett-Detig and Hartl, 2012; Balanyá et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: In African Anopheles, inversion polymorphism is thought to enable fine-grained adaptation of malaria vectors to diverse ecological conditions.
source: In African Anopheles, inversion polymorphism is thought to enable fine-grained adaptation of malaria vectors to diverse ecological conditions, thus expanding the range of an important malaria vector throughout Africa (Coluzzi et al., 1979).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Vector control tools that target indoor-resting mosquitoes, such as bednets and insecticides, are currently the cornerstone of malaria control in Africa.
source: Vector control tools that target indoor-resting mosquitoes, such as bednets and insecticides, are currently the cornerstone of malaria control in Africa.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about current malaria control strategies.

claim: Populations with high levels of the 2L+a allele may form reservoirs of persistent outdoor malaria transmission requiring novel measures for surveillance and control.
source: Populations with high levels of the 2L+a allele may form reservoirs of persistent outdoor malaria transmission requiring novel measures for surveillance and control.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on the observed association of 2L+a with susceptibility and exophilic behavior.

claim: The 2La inversion is a major and previously unappreciated component of the natural malaria transmission system in Africa.
source: The 2La inversion is a major and previously unappreciated component of the natural malaria transmission system in Africa, influencing both malaria susceptibility and vector behavior.
evidence: This is a summary claim based on the findings of the study.

claim: In Kenya, mosquitoes were collected from 10 villages in Nyanza Province near Lake Victoria during the main rainy seasons of 2002 and 2003.
source: In Kenya, mosquitoes were collected from 10 villages in Nyanza Province near Lake Victoria as described (Prugnolle et al., 2008; Razakandrainibe et al., 2005). Briefly, indoor-resting, bloodfed females were collected with aspirators from dwellings in the morning during the main rainy seasons of 2002 and 2003 (mid-March to June).
evidence: This describes the methods used for mosquito collection in Kenya.

claim: In Guinea-Conakry, indoor-resting mosquitoes were collected between 06:00 and 12:00 hr in semi-forest and deep forest sites during May 2008.
source: In the Republic of Guinea (Guinea-Conakry), indoor-resting mosquitoes were collected with aspirators between 06:00 and 12:00 hr in semi-forest (Kenemabomba and Koraboh) and deep forest (Koundara) sites during May 2008.
evidence: This describes the methods used for mosquito collection in Guinea-Conakry.

claim: In Burkina Faso, wild larvae were collected, raised to adults in the insectary, and fed on gametocytemic blood from naturally infected volunteers.
source: In Burkina Faso, wild larvae were collected by dipping from breeding sites in the region of Goundry, raised to adults in the insectary, and were fed on gametocytemic blood from naturally infected volunteers from the Goundry vicinity, as previously described (Riehle et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the methods used for mosquito collection and infection in Burkina Faso.

claim: The raw P. falciparum infection prevalence in Guinea-Conakry collection was 3.3%.
source: In the Guinea-Conakry collection, raw P. falciparum infection prevalence was 3.3% (for the presence of any parasite stage as detected by molecular assay), and represented completely unfiltered wild-collected samples, in which some mosquitoes did not take any bloodmeal, or did not feed on a gametocyte carrier, or fed too recently to develop oocysts.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the raw infection prevalence in the Guinea-Conakry samples.

claim: The raw oocyst infection prevalence in Kenya collection was 25.5%.
source: In the Kenya collection, raw oocyst infection prevalence was 25.5%, and represented wild mosquitoes filtered for the presence of bloodmeal and then incubated in the insectary for 7-day post-capture to allow oocysts, if present, to develop.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the raw infection prevalence in the Kenya samples.

claim: In the Burkina Faso samples, the raw oocyst infection prevalence was 54%.
source: In contrast, in the Burkina Faso samples, which were membrane-fed on infectious wild gametocytes and unfed mosquitoes removed, the raw oocyst infection prevalence was 54%, and thus all mosquitoes were directly used as the association test set.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the raw infection prevalence in the Burkina Faso samples.

claim: Endophilic mosquitoes both bite and rest indoors.
source: Exophilic mosquitoes tend to rest outdoors to digest the bloodmeal and complete their gonotrophic cycle, although they may bite either outdoors or indoors, while endophilic mosquitoes both bite and rest indoors (Bockarie et al., 1993; Coluzzi et al., 1977; Gillies, 1956; Riehle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mosquito behavior, supported by citations.

claim: Exophilic mosquitoes tend to rest outdoors to digest the bloodmeal and complete their gonotrophic cycle, although they may bite either outdoors or indoors.
source: Exophilic mosquitoes tend to rest outdoors to digest the bloodmeal and complete their gonotrophic cycle, although they may bite either outdoors or indoors, while endophilic mosquitoes both bite and rest indoors (Bockarie et al., 1993; Coluzzi et al., 1977; Gillies, 1956; Riehle et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mosquito behavior, supported by citations.

claim: Endophilic mosquitoes are efficiently sampled by capture of house-resting mosquitoes within enclosed spaces.
source: Endophilic mosquitoes are efficiently sampled by capture of house-resting mosquitoes within the enclosed space using pyrethroid spray or aspirator, while sampling methods for exophilic mosquitoes are inefficient because the outdoor resting sites are spatially scattered at largely uncharacterized sites anywhere in the outdoor environment (Gillies, 1956, 1954).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mosquito sampling methods, supported by citations.

claim: Sampling methods for exophilic mosquitoes are inefficient because outdoor resting sites are spatially scattered at largely uncharacterized sites.
source: Endophilic mosquitoes are efficiently sampled by capture of house-resting mosquitoes within the enclosed space using pyrethroid spray or aspirator, while sampling methods for exophilic mosquitoes are inefficient because the outdoor resting sites are spatially scattered at largely uncharacterized sites anywhere in the outdoor environment (Gillies, 1956, 1954).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about mosquito sampling methods, supported by citations.

claim: Most knowledge of A. gambiae behavior indicates strong human-feeding propensity.
source: First, most knowledge of A. gambiae behavior to date indicates strong human-feeding propensity (Costantini and Diallo, 2001; Garrett-Jones et al., 1980; Gillies and Coetzee, 1987; White, 1974; Pates et al., 2001), with very few accounts of zoophily (Diatta et al., 1998; Duchemin et al., 2001), so an exclusively zoophilic group within A. gambiae would be unexpected.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Females preferentially choose oviposition sites that maximize survival of larval progeny.
source: This argument is unconvincing for several reasons, including (i) the above data that 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes do not display lower survival, and are not immunologically weaker than 2La/2La, (ii) evidence that females preferentially choose oviposition sites that maximize survival of larval progeny (Diabaté et al., 2008; Munga et al., 2006; Suh et al., 2016), and (iii) if 2L+a/2L+a larvae consistently displayed elevated mortality in nature, it would be difficult to explain the observed frequencies of a genotype with high negative fitness load.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The previous study of 2La inversion and P. falciparum infection found that higher rate of CSP-positives in 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes was observed in the midgut, head-thorax, and salivary glands.
source: The previous study of the 2La inversion and P. falciparum infection, using wild-caught A. gambiae in Kenya with cytogenetic karyotyping of 2La and circumsporozoite protein (CSP) immunoassay for parasite detection, found that the higher rate of CSP-positives in 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes was observed in the mosquito midgut, head-thorax, and salivary glands (Petrarca and Beier, 1992).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The higher prevalence of midgut oocyst infection in 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes was translated into sporozoites and a higher prevalence of infectious mosquitoes with positive salivary glands.
source: This indicates that the higher prevalence of midgut oocyst infection was translated into sporozoites, and therefore a higher prevalence of infectious 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes with positive salivary glands.
evidence: This is an inference based on the previous study's findings about CSP-positives in different mosquito tissues.

claim: Mosquitoes become infectious for malaria transmission only when sporozoites invade the salivary glands 12-14 days after the infective bloodmeal.
source: Moreover, if the more infected 2L+a/2L+a mosquitoes die sooner than 2La/2La individuals, regardless of the cause, then the epidemiological impact of the 2La inversion effect on susceptibility could be diminished, because infected mosquitoes become infectious for malaria transmission only when sporozoites invade the salivary glands 12–14 days after the infective bloodmeal.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the malaria parasite development timeline in mosquitoes.

claim: In nature most mosquitoes carry less than 5 oocysts.
source: In nature most mosquitoes carry <5 oocysts (Pringle, 1966).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Entomopathogenic fungi are model eukaryotic pathogens used in studies of mosquito immunity and are a proposed biopesticide for vector control.
source: Entomopathogenic fungi are model eukaryotic pathogens used in studies of mosquito immunity and are a proposed biopesticide for vector control (Dong and Dimopoulos, 2009; Thomas and Read, 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Evidence is lacking that Plasmodium imposes a fitness cost upon infected mosquitoes in nature.
source: However, evidence is lacking that Plasmodium imposes a fitness cost upon infected mosquitoes in nature, and deleterious effects of Plasmodium are mainly seen using artificial vector-parasite combinations or unnatural infection levels (Ahmed and Hurd, 2006; Ferguson and Read, 2002; Robert et al., 1990; Zhao et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Larval pools are a limiting resource for female oviposition.
source: Larval pools are a limiting resource for female oviposition, and collection of larvae thus provides an unbiased measure of overall population genotype frequencies, independent of adult mosquito behavior or resting site preference (Fillinger and Lindsay, 2011; Gordicho et al., 2014; Riehle et al., 2011; Killeen et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Collection of larvae provides an unbiased measure of overall population genotype frequencies, independent of adult mosquito behavior or resting site preference.
source: Larval pools are a limiting resource for female oviposition, and collection of larvae thus provides an unbiased measure of overall population genotype frequencies, independent of adult mosquito behavior or resting site preference (Fillinger and Lindsay, 2011; Gordicho et al., 2014; Riehle et al., 2011; Killeen et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The core habitats of 2L+a carrying mosquitoes appear to be ecologically synonymous with the foci or hotspots of the most stable, endemic core transmission of African P. falciparum.
source: Thus, the core habitats of 2L+a carrying mosquitoes appear to be ecologically synonymous with the foci or hotspots of the most stable, endemic core transmission of African P. falciparum.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between 2L+a frequency, humidity, and high PfPR zones.

claim: Under favorable ecological conditions for both vectors and PfPR, transmission levels may be saturating, and variation in vectorial capacity may not be the most important limiting factor for PfPR.
source: Under such favorable ecological conditions for both vectors and PfPR, transmission levels may be saturating, and variation in vectorial capacity may not be the most important limiting factor for PfPR (Brady et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by citation and inference.

claim: Human short-duration immunity maintained by frequent exposure to infectious bites may contribute more strongly to defining the upper limit of PfPR under current conditions.
source: Under the current conditions, human short-duration immunity maintained by frequent exposure to infectious bites may contribute more strongly to defining the upper limit of PfPR (Langhorne et al., 2008; Smith et al., 2006; Tran et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by citations.

claim: The current regions of high PfPR, 2L+a frequency, and humidity are some of the economically poorest and geographically remote areas where malaria control has been less consistently implemented.
source: The current regions of high PfPR, 2L+a frequency, and humidity are also some of the economically poorest and geographically remote, where malaria control has been less consistently implemented (Tiffany et al., 2016; Bhatt et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: As sustained malaria control interventions depress vector populations and baseline PfPR, the more susceptible and exophilic 2L+a vectors may begin to disproportionately mediate residual transmission.
source: However, as sustained malaria control interventions at these high-PfPR foci depress vector populations and baseline PfPR, the more susceptible and exophilic 2L+a vectors may begin to disproportionately mediate residual transmission.
evidence: This is a speculative claim based on inference from the study findings.
